subject: environmental-science
title: Food Chains & Webs: Webs & Pyramids
welcome_lead: Real ecosystems are webs — every species linked to many others.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: food webs, trophic levels, pyramids.
final_note: Pull one strand and the whole web shivers.

concepts.def: Shows numbers, biomass or energy at each level.
Top predator with no natural enemies.

walkthroughs.body_html: Most animals eat several things. Link many chains and you get a food web showing the real picture.
Each step is a trophic level. Energy is lost at each step (often only 10% passes on). That's why apex predators are rare.
An energy pyramid shows how much energy passes on. Producers at the bottom; apex predators at the top.

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Because warming is positive (a good thing).
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Because polar bears help spread heat.

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Because polar bears help spread heat.
